mainTopic: Unusual births and miscarriages: the two-backed child, animals born early, fetuses shaped like a לילית or a snake, and a miscarried sac, followed by אבא שאול's stories about giant bones.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רב and שמואל about a creature with two backs and two spines. שמואל reads a ברייתא about animals to fit his view, and רב adds the two-backed child to a ברייתא that says only a baby fit for a ברית on the eighth day brings טומאת לידה. רב הונא rules that in practice we follow רב, because the הלכה follows רב in איסורים. Next, רבא asks whether a large animal can give birth to a living calf at seven months, like a woman. A proof is suggested and then pushed off, and the question stays unproven. Then come rulings and a story about miscarried fetuses shaped like a לילית or a snake, ending with אביי's lesson that a scholar should always give the reason for his ruling. A new משנה follows about a miscarried sac, and the גמרא gives three answers for why a sac of colors is not a dissolved child. Finally, אבא שאול's gravedigger stories about huge bones lead into a chain of each generation's tallest man, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל reads the animal ברייתא to fit his view
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains the ברייתא about premature animals so it matches his opinion: a two-backed animal is forbidden only if it came out into the world, but permitted if found inside its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל explains the ברייתא his way. A small animal born in its fourth month, or a large animal born in its eighth month, or anything born even earlier, is forbidden. When is that true? Only when it did not finish its months. If it did finish its months, it is permitted. But the two-backed animal is different: even if it finished its months, it is forbidden once it comes out into the world, though it is permitted while still inside its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל takes a ברייתא that seemed to support רב and reads it so it fits his own view about the two-backed animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the two-backed animal as forbidden. רב took this to mean it is always forbidden. שמואל says the ברייתא only forbids it after it comes out into the world. While still inside its mother, it is permitted together with the mother, so the ברייתא is not a problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains the source according to his own reasoning
Its months of pregnancy were completed (it was born at full term)
The open air of the world, meaning after it was born

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the two-backed animal is always fine. He agrees it is forbidden once it is born. He only permits it while it is still inside its mother.

phrases.english: And Shmuel explains it according to his reasoning:
born in the fourth month, for small animals,
born in the eighth month, for large animals —
from that point and earlier, it is forbidden.
In what case are these words said?
When its months were not completed,
but if its months were completed, it is permitted.
This excludes one that has
two backs and two spines,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּכָלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו —
phrases.english: for even though its months were completed,
if it came out into the air of the world, it is forbidden,
but in its mother's womb, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from earlier on the דף, where רב read the same ברייתא in support of his view. Now שמואל gives his own reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the ban on the two-backed animal is limited to after it is born.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid the two-backed animal in every case, which would match רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids it only after it has come out into the world. Inside its mother it is permitted, which fits שמואל.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a shapeless miscarriage does not make the mother impure from birth
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב. A woman who miscarries a creature without a clear body or head shape is not טמאה לידה, because the פסוק links birth impurity to a child fit for ברית מילה on the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רב: If a woman miscarries a body with no clear shape, or a head with no clear shape, you might think she is impure as a woman who gave birth. So the פסוק says, "A woman who conceives and gives birth to a male... and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised." This means a child who could live to have a ברית on the eighth day. These creatures, who could not, are left out.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is taught that limits טומאת לידה to a child who could survive until a ברית on the eighth day. This sets up רב's addition in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the closeness of the two פסוקים: the birth-impurity verse is right next to the ברית מילה verse. So only a birth that could reach a ברית counts. A shapeless creature cannot survive that long, so the mother does not get טומאת לידה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries or discharges a fetus
A body form without shaped limbs
Impure with the impurity of a woman after childbirth
"One might think": a setup for what the פסוק will rule out
Fit for circumcision on the eighth day, meaning able to survive that long

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav:
phrases.notes: A תנא here is someone whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות.

phrases.english: A woman who miscarries a body form that is not shaped,
phrases.notes: "Not shaped" means you cannot make out separate limbs.

phrases.english: or a head form that is not shaped,
one might think its mother should be impure from childbirth?
So the verse teaches:
"A woman who conceives and gives birth to a male, etc.
and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised, etc."
meaning one who is fit for circumcision on the eighth day,
which leaves out these
that are not fit for circumcision on the eighth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from animals to women, bringing a ברייתא recited before רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a child who could survive to a ברית on the eighth day brings טומאת לידה. A shapeless miscarriage does not.

steps.title: רב adds the two-backed child to the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב tells the תנא to finish the ברייתא by adding the two-backed, two-spined child to the list of births that do not bring טומאת לידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב told him: Finish the ברייתא this way: "and also one that has two backs and two spines."
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds his own view into the ברייתא: a child with two backs and two spines also cannot survive to the eighth day, so it does not count as a birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches what רב said earlier: for a woman, such a child is not a ולד. The reason he can add it here is the eighth-day rule just learned, since this child is not fit for a ברית on the eighth day.

keyTerms.meaning: And finish it like this, meaning add these words at the end

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows רב's view in practice: a woman who gives birth to a two-backed child does not get the laws of a woman after childbirth. This sets up the practical question that follows.

phrases.english: Rav said to him:
And finish it like this:

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּין וּשְׁנֵי שִׁדְרָאוֹת.
phrases.english: "and one that has two backs and two spines."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב וְסַיֵּים בַּהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the two-backed case to the ברייתא from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, a child with two backs and two spines is not a ולד, so the mother is not טמאה לידה.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא wants to rule like שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא planned to rule in a real case like שמואל, that a two-backed child counts as a birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא thought to rule in practice like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: A real case comes up, and רבי ירמיה בר אבא plans to follow שמואל. This sets up רב הונא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following שמואל means the woman becomes טמאה לידה. That looks like the stricter choice, since under רב she would not get birth impurity at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To act in a real case, meaning to give a practical ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba thought
to rule in practice like Shmuel,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא סָבַר לְמֶעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources to a practical ruling between רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He planned to treat the two-backed child as a real birth, following שמואל.

steps.title: רב הונא: being strict here leads to a leniency
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges him: following שמואל to be strict actually brings a leniency, because a woman after birth gets days of דם טוהר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: What are you thinking, that you want to be strict? This strictness leads to a leniency, because you are giving her days of pure blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shows that following שמואל is not really the safe, strict choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the child counts as a birth, then after her days of impurity the woman enters days of דם טוהר. During those days, blood she sees is pure. Under רב, that same blood would make her a נדה. So the "strict" ruling ends up being lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency that leads to a leniency
Blood of purity: blood seen in the days after the impurity of birth, which does not make her impure

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's view is stricter at first, since she becomes impure from birth. But it is more lenient later, since her bleeding is treated as דם טוהר. That is why you cannot simply call it "the strict view."

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to him:
What is your thinking, to be strict?
It is a stringency that leads to a leniency,
since you are giving her days of pure blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plan in step 4 to follow שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's choice to follow שמואל as the stricter view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling it a birth also gives her days of דם טוהר, so blood that would make her a נדה under רב is pure. The ruling is not purely strict.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב in prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that one should follow רב, because the הלכה follows רב in איסורים, whether that leads to leniency or strictness.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, rule like רב, because we hold that the הלכה follows רב in matters of prohibition, whether that is lenient or strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the final practical ruling: follow רב, so the two-backed child is not a real birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since you cannot be strict both ways, rely on the general rule that the הלכה follows רב against שמואל in איסורים. So the woman does not get טומאת לידה or days of דם טוהר.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, as an established rule
The הלכה follows רב in matters of prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: A child with two backs and two spines is not a ולד, following רב. The mother gets no טומאת לידה and no days of דם טוהר. The reason: the הלכה follows רב in איסורים, even when one might try to be strict like שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that the הלכה follows רב in איסורים and שמואל in דינים (money matters), is a classic rule for deciding between רב and שמואל throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: At any rate, rule like Rav,
for we hold that the halacha follows Rav in matters of prohibition,
whether to leniency or to stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב הונא's challenge with the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice we follow רב: a two-backed, two-spined child does not count as a birth for טומאת לידה, because the הלכה follows רב in איסורים.

steps.title: רבא asks whether a large animal can give birth after seven months
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes that a woman can give birth to a living child at nine months or at seven months. A large animal gives birth at nine months. He asks whether a large animal can also give birth to a living offspring at seven months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The חכמים taught that a woman gives birth at nine months and also at seven months. A large animal gives birth at nine months. Can it also give birth at seven months, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question: does the rule that a woman can have a living baby at seven months also apply to a large animal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman and a large animal both have a normal nine-month pregnancy. For a woman, a seven-month birth can also produce a living baby. רבא wants to know whether the animal follows the same pattern or only gives birth to a living offspring at the full nine months.

keyTerms.meaning: A large domesticated animal, like a cow
Behold, the חכמים said: introduces an accepted teaching

phrases.english: Rava said:
Behold, they said:
a woman gives birth at nine months
and gives birth at seven months;
a large animal gives birth at nine months.
Does it give birth at seven months, or does it not give birth?
phrases.notes: 'Give birth' here means having an offspring that can live.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ, אִשָּׁה יוֹלֶדֶת לְתִשְׁעָה וְיוֹלֶדֶת לְשִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the ruling about following רב in איסורים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a large animal can give birth to a living offspring after only seven months, like a woman.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a proof from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes a ברייתא: an animal born 'from this point and below' is אסור. He suggests the ברייתא is talking about a large animal, which would show that a large animal born early cannot live.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Come and hear. 'From this point and below, it is forbidden.' Isn't this talking about a large animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק tries to answer רבא's question with a ruling from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says an animal born before its full time is forbidden, because it is treated as one that could never live. If this refers to a large animal, then a large animal born at seven months cannot live, unlike a human baby. That would answer רבא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: From this point and below: born earlier than this stage
Forbidden. Here it means forbidden to eat.
Isn't it? Introduces a suggested reading meant to prove a point

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Come and hear:
From this point and below, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: He means an animal that comes out before its full term is forbidden to eat.

phrases.english: Is it not referring to a large animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבא's question.
steps.raayaObject: That a large animal born at seven months cannot live.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that an animal born before its full term is forbidden, read as referring to a large animal.

steps.title: The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא may be about small animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא may be talking about a small animal, not a large one, so it proves nothing about large animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to a small animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the ברייתא as being about small animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about small animals like sheep and goats, it says nothing about cows. Then רבא's question about large animals is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: A small domesticated animal, like a sheep or goat

phrases.english: No, it refers to a small animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reading that the ברייתא is about large animals.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could be talking about small animals, so it proves nothing about large ones.

steps.title: Challenging the pushback: about small animals the ruling would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the ברייתא is about small animals. About large animals the ruling needs to be taught, because we might compare them to a woman. About small animals the ruling is obvious, since a fetus at three months clearly cannot live.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? If you say it refers to a large animal, the ruling is needed. You might have thought that since a woman's baby lives at seven months, an animal's offspring also lives. So it teaches us that it does not live. But if you say it was said about a small animal, that is obvious! Can a three-month-old fetus live?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the pushback from step 9. A ברייתא does not teach something obvious, so it must be about large animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a large animal there is a real reason to be confused, because a woman with the same nine-month pregnancy can have a living baby at seven months. So the ברייתא has to tell us the animal is different. For a small animal, the early stage is only about three months, and no one would think that could live, so teaching it would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? Opens a challenge to the last statement
It makes sense: one option works well, unlike the other
It is needed: the teaching has a purpose
You might have thought: the mistaken idea the teaching prevents
It teaches us: the new point being taught
Obvious! Why would this need to be taught?

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא does not bother teaching something obvious. That is why the 'it is needed' versus 'it is obvious' test matters. Here it tries to push the ברייתא back to large animals, but the next step answers this challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: The early stage for a small animal is about three months, not seven. Small animals carry for a much shorter time, so the parallel early stage is much shorter too.

phrases.english: What is this?
It makes sense if you say it refers to a large animal:
it is needed,
since it would enter your mind to say:
since with a woman, the baby lives,
with an animal too, it lives.
So it teaches us that it does not live.
But if you say
it was stated about a small animal,
that is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: בַּת תְּלָתָא יַרְחֵי מִי קָא חָיֵי?!
phrases.english: Can a three-month-old live?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא אַגַּסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the pushback of step 9 and supports reading the ברייתא as being about large animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that the ברייתא refers to small animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא would not teach something obvious. About small animals the ruling is obvious, since a three-month fetus cannot live. Only about large animals is it needed, because we might compare them to a woman's seven-month birth.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge stands, the ברייתא is about large animals, and that answers רבא's question: a large animal born at seven months does not live.

steps.title: The ruling about small animals is needed after all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא must teach the rule for small animals. Otherwise we would think any animal born two months before its full term survives.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. You might have thought that any animal born two months early survives, so the ברייתא teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10, which said that a ruling about small animals would be obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman can give birth to a living child at seven months, which is two months early. So we might have thought the rule is 'two months early is fine' for every animal. A small animal born at three months is also two months early, so the ברייתא needs to tell us it does not survive.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (this teaching is needed)
It would enter your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about an animal born 'from this point and below' can be talking about small animals. It teaches that the 'two months early' rule we know from a woman does not apply to them. So it gives no proof about large animals.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
it would enter your mind to say:
any animal born two months short of full term survives,
so it teaches us that it does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 and keeps the דחיה of Step 9 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the teaching is needed, because of a mistaken first thought
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal born two months before full term survives, just like a woman at seven months.
steps.terutzMaskana: A small animal born two months early does not survive. The ברייתא can be about small animals, so it does not settle the question about large animals.

steps.title: A fetus shaped like a לילית counts as a birth
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a woman who miscarries a fetus shaped like a לילית is טמאה לידה, because it is a real child that simply has wings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A woman who miscarries something shaped like a לילית is impure as after childbirth. It is a child, it just has wings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling from שמואל about a miscarried fetus with an unusual shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לילית has a human face and wings. Since the main form is human, the wings do not take it out of the category of a human child. So the mother has the טומאה of a woman who gave birth.

keyTerms.meaning: A female demon with a human face and wings
Impure with the impurity of a woman after childbirth

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A woman who miscarries a fetus shaped like a lilith,
its mother is impure as after childbirth,

phrases.aramaic: וָלָד הוּא אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כְּנָפַיִם.
phrases.english: for it is a child, only it has wings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַמַּפֶּלֶת דְּמוּת לִילִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of animals born early ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miscarried fetus shaped like a לילית is a child, so the mother is טמאה לידה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל with a real case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי יוסי told of a case in סימוניא. The חכמים ruled there that a fetus shaped like a לילית is a child with wings, just as שמואל said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. רבי יוסי said: There was a case in סימוניא where a woman miscarried something shaped like a לילית. The case came before the חכמים, and they said it is a child, it just has wings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of the חכמים in the ברייתא uses the same words as שמואל: 'it is a child, only it has wings.' This shows that שמואל's ruling is based on an older, actual decision.

keyTerms.meaning: סימוניא, the name of a town

phrases.english: It is also taught in a baraita this way:
Rabbi Yosei said,
there was an incident in Simonya
with a woman who miscarried a fetus shaped like a lilith,
and the case came before the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ: וָלָד הוּא אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כְּנָפַיִם.
phrases.english: and they said: It is a child, only it has wings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the מימרא of Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a לילית-shaped fetus is a child, so the mother is טמאה לידה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording an actual case in סימוניא decided by the חכמים

steps.title: חנינא rules about a snake-shaped fetus and is summoned
steps.stepSummary: חנינא, the nephew of רבי יהושע, ruled that a woman who miscarried something shaped like a snake is טמאה לידה. רבי יוסף reported this to רבן גמליאל, who told רבי יהושע to bring his nephew to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman miscarried something shaped like a snake. חנינא, the nephew of רבי יהושע, ruled that the mother is impure as after childbirth. רבי יוסף went and told this to רבן גמליאל. רבן גמליאל sent a message to רבי יהושע: 'Bring your nephew and come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a ruling on a snake-shaped fetus. This step sets up the scene for what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A snake is much less human-looking than a לילית, so חנינא's ruling seemed surprising. That is why it was reported to רבן גמליאל. He summoned חנינא together with his uncle, apparently to question the ruling.

phrases.english: A woman who miscarries something shaped like a snake:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרָה חֲנִינָא בֶּן אָחִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Chanina, the son of Rabbi Yehoshua's brother, ruled:
Its mother is impure as after childbirth.
Rabbi Yosef went and told the matter
before Rabban Gamliel,
and he sent a message to Rabbi Yehoshua:
phrases.notes: The one sending here is רבן גמליאל. He is sending the message to רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Bring your nephew along and come.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפֶּלֶת דְּמוּת נָחָשׁ, הוֹרָה חֲנִינָא בֶּן אָחִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the לילית shape to a less human shape, a snake, told through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנינא ruled that a woman who miscarries a snake-shaped fetus is טמאה לידה.

steps.title: On the way, חנינא's daughter-in-law asks רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: While they were traveling, חנינא's daughter-in-law came out and asked רבי יהושע about a snake-shaped fetus. He answered that the mother is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: While they were going, חנינא's daughter-in-law came out to meet him. She said: 'רבי, what is the law for a woman who miscarries something like a snake?' He said to her: 'Its mother is pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues on the road. רבי יהושע is asked the same question and answers the opposite of what חנינא ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יהושע himself says the mother is pure. This seems to make חנינא's ruling even more of a problem. It also sets up the daughter-in-law's surprise in the next step.

phrases.english: While they were going,
Chanina's daughter-in-law came out to greet him,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, 'רבי', and some leave it out. Either way, she is חנינא's daughter-in-law.

phrases.english: she said to him: My teacher,
what is the law for a woman who miscarries something like a snake?
He said to her: Its mother is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. רבי יהושע gives a ruling that seems to go against חנינא's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law for a woman who miscarries something shaped like a snake?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע answers that the mother is pure.

steps.title: She reminds him that he once said the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The daughter-in-law objects. Her mother-in-law had quoted רבי יהושע as saying the mother is טמאה, and as giving the reason that a snake's eyeball is round like a human's.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: 'But my mother-in-law told me in your name that the mother is impure! And she said you told her the reason: because its eyeball is round like a person's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The daughter-in-law challenges רבי יהושע's answer using his own earlier words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She does not just report the ruling. She also gives the reason he once said: the snake's eyeball is round like a human's. That detail ties the fetus to a human form, so it counts as a child.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא מִשִּׁמְךָ אָמְרָה לִי חֲמוֹתִי
phrases.english: She said to him: But did my mother-in-law not tell me in your name
that its mother is impure?
And you said to her: For what reason?
phrases.notes: She is still quoting her mother-in-law. This is what רבי יהושע had told the mother-in-law back then.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְגַלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.english: Because its eyeball is round like that of a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע's answer in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's statement that the mother is pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He himself once ruled that the mother is טמאה, and he gave a reason for it. So how can he now say she is pure?

steps.title: רבי יהושע remembers and defends חנינא
steps.stepSummary: Because of her words, רבי יהושע remembered his earlier ruling. He sent a message to רבן גמליאל that חנינא had ruled based on what he learned from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of her words, רבי יהושע remembered. He sent a message to רבן גמליאל: 'חנינא ruled based on what he heard from me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי יהושע remembers that the ruling was really his own, and he clears his nephew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנינא had not made up a strange ruling. He was faithfully repeating his uncle's teaching, which rests on the human-like round eyeball. The story clears חנינא of ruling on his own. It does not report a final decision on the law itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From my mouth (based on my teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: A fetus shaped like a לילית counts as a child, since it is human-shaped and only has wings (שמואל and the חכמים). For a snake-shaped fetus, the story shows that חנינא's ruling of טמאה came from רבי יהושע, who based it on the round, human-like eyeball.

phrases.english: Because of her words, Rabbi Yehoshua remembered,
and he sent a message to Rabban Gamliel:
Chanina ruled based on my own words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the challenge of Step 16. רבי יהושע accepts his earlier ruling and backs חנינא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חנינא's ruling came from רבי יהושע himself, who had once ruled that a snake-shaped fetus makes the mother טמאה because its eyeball is round like a human's.

steps.title: אביי's lesson: always give the reason for your ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the story that a scholar should say the reason for a ruling, so a reminder of the reason will bring the ruling back to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that a Torah scholar who gives a ruling should give its reason too. Then, when people remind him of it, he will remember.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story of רבי יהושע with a practical lesson from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had forgotten his own ruling. He only remembered it when the daughter-in-law repeated his reason about the snake's round eyeball. So אביי teaches that saying the reason works like a memory hook.
steps.whatToRemember: The snake story ends with a lesson: giving the reason for a ruling helps the scholar himself remember it later.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this,
that a Torah scholar who says a ruling
should say the reason along with it,
so that when they remind him, he will remember.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from how the story ended in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A scholar should state the reason for his ruling, because a reminder of the reason will bring back the ruling.

steps.title: משנה: a sac with fluid, a formed sac, a sandal, or an afterbirth
steps.stepSummary: A sac full of water, blood, or colors is not a child. A sac with formed tissue, a סנדל, or a שליא does count as a birth, and she keeps the rules for both a boy and a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who miscarries a sac full of water, full of blood, or full of colors does not need to worry that it was a child. But if the sac had formed tissue, she keeps the rules for both a boy and a girl. A woman who miscarries a sandal-shaped fetus or an afterbirth keeps the rules for both a boy and a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sorts things a woman might miscarry into ones that count as a birth and ones that don't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An empty-looking sac with only liquid inside is not a child, so there is no טומאת לידה. A sac with real tissue is treated as a child. Since we can't tell if it was a boy or a girl, she takes the stricter side of each. She is טמאה for fourteen days like a girl, and her days of pure blood last only forty days like a boy.

keyTerms.meaning: The sac that holds a fetus
Colors (here, a sac filled with different colored matter)
She keeps the rules of both a boy and a girl
A flat fetus shaped like a sandal fish

steps.confusionAlert: "Sits for male and female" does not mean she counts the days twice. She takes whichever rule is stricter from each: fourteen טמא days like a girl, but pure-blood days only up to forty like a boy.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A woman who miscarries a sac full of water,
full of blood, or full of colors,
does not need to worry that it was a child.
But if the sac had formed tissue,
she keeps the rules for both a boy and a girl.
A woman who miscarries a sandal-shaped fetus or an afterbirth
keeps the rules for both a boy and a girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sac with only liquid inside is not a child. A formed sac, a סנדל, or a שליא counts as a birth of unknown gender.

steps.title: Why not worry that a child dissolved in the colored sac?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that water and blood are nothing. But it asks why a sac of colors isn't treated as a child that dissolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense with blood and water, because those are nothing. But colors? Let us worry that maybe it was a child and it dissolved!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one part of the משנה: the case of a sac full of colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water and blood clearly aren't a child. But colored matter might be what is left of a fetus that broke down. So why does the משנה say she doesn't need to worry? The next three steps each answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense with... (sets up a "but what about" challenge)

phrases.english: Gemara:
It makes sense with blood and water,
because that is nothing.
But colors?
Let us worry that maybe it was a child and it dissolved!

steps.triggerLanguage: בשלמא דם ומים לא כלום היא אלא גנינים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the third case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a sac full of colors is not a child.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Colored matter could be a fetus that broke down, so we should be worried about it.

steps.title: אביי: fetuses don't just dissolve
steps.stepSummary: אביי mocks the worry: a fetus does not normally dissolve in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How much undiluted wine did this one's mother drink, that her fetus dissolved inside her womb?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge with a rhetorical question: that kind of thing just doesn't happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only something extreme, like drinking a lot of strong wine, might destroy a fetus. In a normal case we don't assume it happened. So the colors are not a dissolved child.

keyTerms.meaning: Undiluted wine (strong, harmful to a fetus)

phrases.english: Abaye said: How much undiluted wine
did the mother of this one drink
that her fetus dissolved inside her womb?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי כמה יין חי שתת אמו של זה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reality-based dismissal: the feared event is too unlikely to worry about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Colored matter might be a dissolved fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fetuses don't dissolve in the womb without some extreme cause, so there is no worry.

steps.title: רבא: the sac is full, so nothing dissolved
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the word "full" that no fetus dissolved, because a dissolved fetus would leave the sac less than full.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We learned "full." If it were true that a fetus dissolved, the sac would be lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer, based on the משנה's word "full."
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dissolved fetus would lose some of its mass, so the sac would not be full anymore. The משנה describes a sac that is completely full. That shows no fetus was there.

phrases.english: Rava said: We learned "full,"
and if it were true that it dissolved,
it would have been lacking.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; it just means 'it would have been'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A full colored sac might hold a dissolved fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: A dissolved fetus would leave the sac lacking. Since it is full, there was no fetus.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: many colors, so nothing dissolved
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה reads the משנה as "colors" and argues that a dissolved fetus would be just one color.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: We learned "colors." If it were true that a fetus dissolved, it would all be one color.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer, based on the fact that the sac has many colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus that broke down would turn into one even color. Since the sac shows different colors, it was never a fetus.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers for why a sac of colors isn't a child: fetuses don't dissolve (אביי), the sac is full (רבא), and there are many colors (רב אדא בר אהבה).

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר: ״גְּוָונִים״ תְּנַן,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: We learned "colors,"
phrases.notes: He reads the משנה's word גנינים as גוונים, "colors," which points to many different shades.

phrases.english: and if it were true that it dissolved,
it would all be one color.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב אדא בר אהבה אמר גוונים תנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different answer to step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The colored matter might be a dissolved fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: A dissolved fetus would be one color. Many colors show it was never a fetus.

steps.title: What bones reveal about drinking and eating
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול, who buried the dead, reports that undiluted wine leaves bones burnt-looking, diluted wine leaves them dark, and proper drinking leaves them full of marrow. The same pattern holds for drinking compared with eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול said: I used to bury the dead, and I would look at their bones. Someone who drank undiluted wine had burnt-looking bones. Someone who drank diluted wine had dark bones. Someone who drank the right way had healthy bones full of marrow. Also, someone who drank more than he ate had burnt bones, someone who ate more than he drank had dark bones, and someone who did both properly had healthy bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where אבא שאול shares what he learned from looking at bones while burying the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives two sets of three. The first set is about how the wine is drunk (strong, watered down, or just right). The second is about the balance between drinking and eating. In both sets, only the balanced way leaves the bones healthy.

phrases.english: It is taught: Abba Shaul says:
I used to bury the dead,
and I would look at the bones of the dead.
One who drinks undiluted wine —
his bones look burnt;
diluted wine — his bones are dark;
properly — his bones are fat with marrow.
And anyone whose drinking is more than his eating —
his bones look burnt;
if his eating is more than his drinking —
his bones are dark;
properly — his bones are fat with marrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא, אבא שאול אומר: קובר מתים הייתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked to אביי's remark in step 21 about the harm of undiluted wine (יַיִן חַי). The גמרא brings אבא שאול's ברייתא on what wine does to the body, which opens a series of his gravedigger stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking strong wine, or drinking more than eating, damages the bones. Balanced habits keep them healthy.

steps.title: Running inside the giant thighbone of עוג
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול (or some say רבי יוחנן) chased a deer into a dead man's thighbone and ran three פרסאות inside it without reaching the end. The sages told him it was the bone of עוג מלך הבשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול (some say רבי יוחנן) said: I used to bury the dead. Once I chased a deer, and I went into the thighbone of a dead person. I ran after the deer for three פרסאות. I never caught the deer, and the bone never ended. When I came back, they told me: that bone belonged to עוג מלך הבשן.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא from אבא שאול tells an amazing story about a gigantic thighbone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bone was so huge that a man could run inside it for miles and still not reach its end. The sages explained that only עוג מלך הבשן, the famous giant, could have had such a bone.

keyTerms.meaning: Parasangs, a long distance measure (about 4 מילין each)
עוג, king of בשן, a famous giant

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: It is taught: Abba Shaul says, and some say it was Rabbi Yochanan:
I used to bury the dead.
Once I ran after a deer,
and I went into the thighbone of a dead person,
and I ran after it for three parasangs,
phrases.notes: He was running the whole way inside the bone.

phrases.aramaic: וּצְבִי לֹא הִגַּעְתִּי, וְקוּלִית לֹא כָּלְתָה.
phrases.english: and I didn't reach the deer, and the thighbone didn't end.
When I came back, they said to me:
It belonged to Og, king of Bashan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא, אבא שאול אומר, ואיתימא רבי יוחנן: קובר מתים הייתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ברייתא in the same series of אבא שאול's gravedigger stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thighbone of עוג מלך הבשן was so huge that a man could run inside it for three פרסאות.

steps.title: Standing inside the eye socket of אבשלום
steps.stepSummary: A burial cave opened under אבא שאול, and he sank into a dead man's eye socket up to his nose. The sages told him it was the eye of אבשלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול said: I used to bury the dead. Once a burial cave opened up under me, and I was standing in the eye socket of a dead person, sunk up to my nose. When I came back, they told me: it was the eye of אבשלום.
steps.whatsHappening: A third ברייתא from אבא שאול tells of a huge eye socket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eye socket was deep enough to hold a grown man up to his nose. The sages identified it as belonging to אבשלום, who was known for his impressive appearance.

keyTerms.meaning: His eyeball, here the eye socket

phrases.english: It is taught: Abba Shaul says:
I used to bury the dead.
Once a cave opened up underneath me,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָמַדְתִּי בְּגַלְגַּל עֵינוֹ שֶׁל מֵת עַד חוֹטְמִי.
phrases.english: and I stood in the eye socket of a dead person up to my nose.
When I came back, they said:
It was the eye of Avshalom.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא, אבא שאול אומר: קובר מתים הייתי. פעם אחת נפתחה מערה תחתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story in the series about giant bones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום's eye socket was deep enough for a man to sink in up to his nose.

steps.title: Maybe אבא שאול was just very short?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא anticipates a doubt: maybe the eye socket only seemed so huge because אבא שאול was a dwarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you would say that אבא שאול was a dwarf...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to the story of the eye socket. It is setting up the next step, which answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אבא שאול were very small, sinking to his nose in an eye socket would not be so amazing. This question tests whether the story really shows how huge אבשלום was.

keyTerms.meaning: And in case you would say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל נַנָּס הֲוָה —
phrases.english: And in case you would say: Abba Shaul was a dwarf —

steps.triggerLanguage: ושמא תאמר: אבא שאול ננס הוה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the force of the eye-socket story in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that אבא שאול sank to his nose in אבשלום's eye socket.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אבא שאול was very short, the eye socket would not have to be extraordinarily large.

steps.title: אבא שאול was the tallest man of his generation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אבא שאול was the tallest of his generation. It then gives a chain: each tallest man of a later generation reached only the shoulder of the tallest man before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. אבא שאול was the tallest man of his generation, and רבי טרפון reached only up to his shoulder. רבי טרפון was the tallest of his generation, and רבי מאיר reached only up to his shoulder. רבי מאיר was the tallest of his generation, and רבי reached only up to his shoulder. רבי was the tallest of his generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that אבא שאול was short. He was actually the tallest man of his time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain shows that people kept getting shorter in each generation. Each generation's tallest man reached only the shoulder of the tallest man before him. So אבא שאול was very tall, and אבשלום's eye socket really was enormous.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'reaches his shoulder' as praise of the shorter person. It means each tallest man was still much shorter than the tallest man of the generation before.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul was the tallest in his generation
and Rabbi Tarfon reached up to his shoulder,
phrases.notes: 'His shoulder' means אבא שאול's shoulder, the person just mentioned.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Tarfon was the tallest in his generation
and Rabbi Meir reached up to his shoulder,
Rabbi Meir was the tallest in his generation
and Rabbi reached up to his shoulder,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Rabbi was the tallest in his generation

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt raised in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual correction: the assumption behind the question is false.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe אבא שאול was a dwarf, so the eye socket was not truly huge.
steps.terutzMaskana: אבא שאול was the tallest of his generation, so the eye socket of אבשלום truly was enormous.

steps.title: The height chain continues from רבי חייא down to אדא דיילא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues its chain: רבי חייא reached the shoulder of the man before him, רב reached רבי חייא's shoulder, רב יהודה reached רב's shoulder, and אדא דיילא reached רב יהודה's shoulder. Each was the tallest of his generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא reached only up to his shoulder, and רבי חייא was the tallest man of his generation. And רב reached only up to רבי חייא's shoulder, and רב was the tallest of his generation. And רב יהודה reached only up to רב's shoulder, and רב יהודה was the tallest of his generation. And אדא the attendant reached only up to רב יהודה's shoulder...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is not starting anything new. It is simply continuing the list from step 28, one generation at a time, to show how much taller the earlier people were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each link has the same two parts. First, 'X reached the shoulder of the one before him.' Then, 'and X was the tallest of his generation.' Because every link is the tallest man of his time, and he still only reaches a shoulder, people keep getting shorter from one generation to the next. That makes אבא שאול, many links earlier, truly huge, so אבשלום's eye socket must have been enormous too.

keyTerms.meaning: Reached up to his shoulder. He was only as tall as the earlier man's shoulder.
The tallest man of his generation
An attendant or servant (someone who serves others)

steps.confusionAlert: 'His shoulder' always means the shoulder of the person named just before, from the previous generation. It never means the shoulder of the person in the same sentence.

phrases.english: And רבי חייא reached up to his shoulder,
and רבי חייא was the tallest in his generation.
And רב reached up to his shoulder,
and רב was the tallest in his generation.
And רב יהודה reached up to his shoulder,
and רב יהודה was the tallest in his generation.
And אדא the attendant reached up to his shoulder,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This directly continues the generational height chain that step 28 began. It adds more links to the same answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual support: a chain of shrinking heights across the generations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe אבא שאול was a dwarf, so the eye socket only seemed huge to him (step 27).
steps.terutzMaskana: אבא שאול was the tallest of his generation, and the chain shows each later tallest man reaching only the shoulder of the one before. So people of earlier times were truly much larger, and the eye socket really was enormous.
